name: Tm Visualization Suite: Comparison Charts
pitch: Compare categories, ranges and ranks in one view, and see who moved and by how much.
question: How do values differ across categories, between two points, or across stages?
useWhen: Compare categories, stages, ranges, or ranks in one view.
features: See the change between two points
Rank many categories on one scale
Draw a stem to the baseline
Show the range, and where you are in it
Compare two stages side by side

hero.alt: Vertical dumbbell chart of net sales for two fiscal years per store, grouped by store format.
hero.caption: Two years per store: who grew, and by how much

screenshots.alt: Dumbbell chart of net sales in two fiscal years for the hypermarkets only, with the change shown beside each store.
screenshots.caption: Select a store format and the dumbbells show only its stores

screenshots.alt: Vertical dot plot of one value per store, grouped by store format.
screenshots.caption: The dot plot also runs upright, for a column-style comparison

questions: Which stores grew most between two years?
How wide is the spread of lead times by region?
Which departments climbed or fell in rank?
audience: Analysts and BI leads who compare categories, periods or stages for a business review.

featureStrips.heading: See the change between two points
featureStrips.text: A dumbbell joins the two values of each category, so a long line means a big change.
featureStrips.alt: Horizontal dumbbell chart of net sales in two fiscal years per store, one outlier with a very long line.

featureStrips.heading: Rank many categories on one scale
featureStrips.text: A dot plot sorts every category on one axis, so the highest and lowest stand out at once.
featureStrips.alt: Dot plot of one value for about forty stores, grouped by store format and sorted from the highest.

featureStrips.heading: Draw a stem to the baseline
featureStrips.text: Add a stem from each dot to the baseline for a lollipop that reads like a lighter bar chart.
featureStrips.alt: Lollipop chart of one value per store with a stem from each dot to the baseline.

featureStrips.heading: Show the range, and where you are in it
featureStrips.text: A range plot draws minimum to maximum with the actual value and the target marked on top.
featureStrips.alt: Range plot of lead time per region, a bar from minimum to maximum with median and target markers.

featureStrips.heading: Compare two stages side by side
featureStrips.text: A slopegraph connects each category between two stages, so risers and fallers show as lines.
featureStrips.alt: Slopegraph per region joining each store between March 2025 and March 2026 with one line per store.

featureStrips.heading: Follow rank across many stages
featureStrips.text: A bump chart tracks the rank of each category over time, so you see who overtakes whom.
featureStrips.alt: Bump chart of nine departments ranked across twelve quarters with one coloured line per department.
